references.text: The same chapter emphasizes that there shall be one law for both the native Israelite and the foreigner living among them.
The principle of one law for the native and the foreigner also applies to the celebration of Passover.
The same law shall apply to the native and to the foreigner living among you - a fundamental principle in the Mosaic Law.
Concerns the sin offering for one who sins unintentionally, the same theme as in Numbers 15:29.
Confirms the principle that the same legal practice applies to the foreigner and to the native.
The contrast to unintentional sin: the one who sins deliberately shall be cut off from their people.
Equality before the law between Israelites and foreigners is also emphasized in the responsibilities of judges.
